name: Elkanah
overview: Elkanah is a male biblical figure known primarily for his role as second to King Ahaz, as noted in 2 Chronicles 28:7. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His mention is brief but indicates a position of significance in the historical context of Israel's monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Elkanah means 'G-d [El] has possessed,' reflecting a theistic acknowledgment embedded in his proper name. This meaning underscores the biblical theme of God's providence and possession, though the name itself was not given directly by God according to the record in 2 Chronicles 28:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Elkanah beyond what is noted in his unique attribute; no further relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elkanah's significance lies in his high-ranking position during the reign of King Ahaz, serving as second in command. This highlights his role within the leadership structure of Israel at a time of political and spiritual challenges. Although details are limited, his mention in 2 Chronicles 28:7 marks him as a noteworthy figure in the biblical historical narrative.
